# bob records

List, inspect, check, and create or update configured Record Notes

```text title="bob records --help"
List, inspect, check, and create or update configured Record Notes

Bare `bob records` runs the read-only list. `new` creates a note through the shared records planner and refuses missing fields or duplicates. `update` edits an existing note in place.

Usage: bob records [COMMAND]

Commands:
  check   Check configured Record Notes against their schemas
  list    List configured Record Note collections (default)
  new     Create one Record Note from its configured schema
  show    Show one record schema and its common values
  update  Update one existing Record Note in place

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Bare `bob records` runs the read-only list.

Examples:
  bob records                                      List record types and counts
  bob records show restaurant                     Inspect a schema and common values
  bob records check -f json                       Lint every configured record folder
  bob records new restaurant 'Ramen Nagi' -s status=to_try

See docs/records.md for the schema, CLI, and lint contract.
Run 'bob records <command> --help' for more information on a command.
```

## bob records check

Check configured Record Notes against their schemas

```text title="bob records check --help"
Lint each configured Record Note folder. Checks the type link, required and typed fields, legacy keys, and records filed outside their configured folder.

Usage: bob records check [OPTIONS] [TYPE]

Arguments:
  [TYPE]
          Configured record type id

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob records check
  bob records check restaurant
  bob records check -f json

See docs/records.md for the schema and lint rules.
```

## bob records list

List configured Record Note collections (default)

```text title="bob records list --help"
Show each configured record type, its folder, note count, and required fields. This command is read-only. Bare `bob records` runs this command.

Usage: bob records list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

Examples:
  bob records
  bob records list
  bob records list -f json

See docs/records.md for record schemas.
```

## bob records new

Create one Record Note from its configured schema

```text title="bob records new --help"
Plan and create a single Record Note. Supply fields with repeated --set KEY=VALUE arguments and notes with repeated --note arguments. Missing required fields are refused with a ready-to-copy draft. --dry-run prints the exact Markdown without writing.

Usage: bob records new [OPTIONS] <TYPE> <TITLE>

Arguments:
  <TYPE>
          Configured record type id

  <TITLE>
          Title of the new record note

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print the planned note without writing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -n, --note <TEXT>
          Append a note bullet; may be repeated

  -o, --open
          Open the created note in Obsidian

  -s, --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Set a configured field; may be repeated

  -S, --stem <STEM>
          Use an explicit filename stem

Examples:
  bob records new restaurant 'Ramen Nagi' -s status=to_try -s category=Ramen -s location=Clark
  bob records new podcast 'The Daily' -s status=to_try -s category=News -n 'Recommended by Kelly' -d
  bob records new restaurant '1950 Originals' -S 1950s_originals -s status=to_try -s category=Pizza -s location=Westwood
  bob records new restaurant 'Ninja Sushi' -d -f json

See docs/records.md for field kinds, defaults, and failure behavior.
```

## bob records update

Update one existing Record Note in place

```text title="bob records update --help"
Resolve an existing record by TYPE and STEM, then edit only the supplied YAML value spans and append notes with repeated --note arguments. Field-only and note-only updates work without repeating required creation fields. --dry-run prints the exact Markdown without writing.

Usage: bob records update [OPTIONS] <TYPE> <STEM>

Arguments:
  <TYPE>
          Configured record type id

  <STEM>
          Existing filename stem of the record note

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <PATH>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -d, --dry-run
          Print the planned note without writing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -n, --note <TEXT>
          Append a note bullet; may be repeated

  -o, --open
          Open the updated note in Obsidian

  -s, --set <KEY=VALUE>
          Set a configured field; may be repeated

Examples:
  bob records update restaurant ninja_sushi -s status=liked -n 'Went back, still great'
  bob records update restaurant ninja_sushi -s location= -d
  bob records update podcast talk_python -n 'Listened to the async episode' -d -f json

See docs/records.md for update semantics, optional clearing, and failure behavior.
```
